decision.question: Should I take a blood thinner (anticoagulant) to reduce my stroke risk?

options.label: Take apixaban (Eliquis) 5 mg twice daily

benefits.outcome: Stroke or blood clot to the body (systemic embolism) prevented

evidence.source: Connolly SJ et al. AVERROES. NEJM 2011; Hart RG et al. Ann Intern Med 2007 (Cochrane meta-analysis); numbers extrapolated to 5-year horizon
evidence.population_caveat: Patients with CHA2DS2-VASc ≥ 2 (moderate-high stroke risk). Stroke rates vary substantially by individual risk score. AVERROES compared to aspirin, not placebo.

harms.outcome: Major bleeding (requiring transfusion, hospitalization, or causing ≥ 2 g/dL hemoglobin drop)

evidence.source: Ruff CT et al. Lancet 2014 (meta-analysis of 4 NOAC trials, n=71,683). Rates vs no anticoagulation estimated from baseline arm of AVERROES.
evidence.population_caveat: Original trials compared to warfarin; absolute rates vs no anticoagulation are estimated. Patient age and kidney function substantially affect bleeding risk.

harms.outcome: Intracranial hemorrhage (bleeding in or around the brain)
harms.cascade: Intracranial hemorrhage has a 30–50% case fatality rate. Survivors frequently have permanent disability affecting movement, speech, or cognition.

evidence.source: Ruff CT et al. Lancet 2014. Apixaban ICH rate substantially lower than warfarin; may be comparable to aspirin.
evidence.population_caveat: Risk is higher in patients with prior stroke, uncontrolled hypertension, or heavy alcohol use.

options.burden: Two capsules daily (morning and evening with or without food). Annual kidney function check recommended. Dose reduces to 2.5 mg twice daily if two or more of: age ≥ 80, weight ≤ 60 kg, creatinine ≥ 1.5 mg/dL. No routine INR blood monitoring required. Cost: approximately $500–600/month without insurance; generic expected 2026–2028.
unknowns: No randomized trial has compared apixaban directly to placebo or no treatment — AVERROES compared to aspirin, which itself reduces stroke somewhat.
Long-term bleeding risk accumulation beyond 5 years is not well characterized in trial follow-up data.
Benefit for patients with CHA2DS2-VASc = 1 (one risk factor) is uncertain; guideline recommendations vary.
Effect in patients over age 85, or with severe kidney disease (eGFR < 25), is not well studied.

options.label: No anticoagulant — watchful waiting

benefits.outcome: Major bleeding avoided (lower bleeding rate than with anticoagulant)

evidence.source: Ruff CT et al. Lancet 2014; Connolly SJ et al. AVERROES. NEJM 2011
evidence.population_caveat: Baseline bleeding rate in untreated AFib population; individual risk varies by age, alcohol use, prior bleeding history, and concomitant medications.

harms.outcome: Stroke or blood clot to the body (untreated — higher rate without anticoagulant)
harms.cascade: Stroke may cause permanent disability affecting speech, mobility, cognition, or swallowing. Risk of a second stroke is substantially elevated after a first event. Systemic embolism may cause limb ischemia requiring amputation.

evidence.source: Hart RG et al. Ann Intern Med 2007 (Cochrane); Connolly SJ et al. AVERROES. NEJM 2011
evidence.population_caveat: CHA2DS2-VASc ≥ 2. Annual stroke risk ranges from approximately 2% (score 2) to 15%+ (score 7+). The 5-year rate here reflects a score of approximately 3.

options.burden: No daily medication required. No blood monitoring required. Continued routine cardiac care. Some clinicians recommend low-dose aspirin as a partial alternative, which carries its own bleeding risk and provides substantially less stroke protection than anticoagulation.
unknowns: Individual stroke risk varies enormously (1–15% per year) based on CHA2DS2-VASc score; population averages may significantly misrepresent your personal risk.
The benefit-harm balance shifts substantially in patients with a prior stroke (much higher baseline risk) or a prior serious bleed (higher harm from treatment).
How falls risk should factor into the decision is not well quantified — retrospective data suggest falls risk is often overweighted as a reason to avoid anticoagulation.
